evals.prompt: /writing-great-skills Review this skill description and tighten it: "description: Helps with test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features using TDD, asks for test-first development, wants to write tests before code, or mentions red-green-refactor. This skill is great for writing tests."
evals.expected_output: The agent rewrites the description by collapsing synonym triggers into distinct branches and cutting identity text, using the skill's vocabulary.
expectations: Identifies that 'TDD', 'test-first development', and 'write tests before code' are duplication of one branch and collapses them
Cuts the no-op/identity sentence ('This skill is great for writing tests')
Front-loads a leading word (e.g. TDD / red-green-refactor) in the rewritten description
Uses the skill's terms such as 'duplication', 'branch', 'context load', or 'leading word' in the explanation

evals.prompt: /writing-great-skills My deploy skill has 9 steps and the agent keeps skipping the verification in step 4 and rushing to step 9 (post the release notes). Step 4 currently says 'Verify the deployment looks good.' How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: The agent diagnoses premature completion and prescribes sharpening the completion criterion first, splitting by sequence only if that fails.
expectations: Names the failure mode as premature completion
First recommends making step 4's completion criterion checkable/exhaustive (e.g. concrete health checks that tell done from not-done) instead of 'looks good'
Mentions splitting by sequence (hiding post-completion steps) only as a second resort if the rush persists after sharpening
Proposes a concrete rewritten step 4 text

evals.prompt: /writing-great-skills I have 12 user-invoked skills now and keep forgetting which exist. Also one of them, 'review', has a SKILL.md that's 600 lines with a big glossary and per-language rules. And it has lines like 'Don't forget to not skip files.' What should I change?
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends a router skill for cognitive load, progressive disclosure for sprawl, and positive phrasing to fix negation/no-op lines.
expectations: Recommends a router skill (one user-invoked skill naming the others and when to use each) to address cognitive load
Diagnoses the 600-line SKILL.md as sprawl and recommends progressive disclosure, e.g. moving the glossary to GLOSSARY.md and per-language rules behind context pointers (branch-based)
Flags 'Don't forget to not skip files' as negation and/or a no-op, and rewrites it positively (e.g. 'Review every changed file')
Does not recommend making the skills model-invoked merely to avoid remembering them without discussing the context-load tradeoff
